thread:
alice.sec: Heads up: new IAM enforcement policy. Starting 2026-07-01 we will block creating new bindings that grant primitive roles (roles/owner, roles/editor) to users and service accounts across org projects. This reduces blast radius and aligns with permission-boundary requirements for production workloads.

alice.sec: Timeline: announcement today; migration window = 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30 for discovery and remediation; enforcement (deny on binding) = 2026-07-01 @ 00:00 UTC. We will run org-wide audits now and open remediation tickets.

alice.sec: Key actions for teams:
- Search for primitive role bindings on your projects: `gcloud projects get-iam-policy PROJECT_ID --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.role=="roles/owner" or .role=="roles/editor")'`
- For service accounts that need wide perms, apply a permission boundary (IAM Conditions + custom role) and document justification.
- Replace primitive role grants with least-privilege custom roles or IAM predefined roles.

alice.sec: Example: create custom role with only required permissions and set a permission boundary for SA:
```
gcloud iam roles create myLimitedRole --project=my-project --permissions="compute.instances.get,compute.instances.list" --title="SRE Limited"
# Add permissionBoundary via policy binding (example of condition-based restriction)
```

alice.sec: If you have many repos using broad roles, consider these quick checks:
- Repo infra: grep for `roles/editor` or `roles/owner` in terraform and YAMLs: `git grep -n "roles/editor"`
- Terraform state: `terraform state list | xargs -n1 terraform state show | grep -E "owner|editor"`
- Cloud audit logs: filter for `SetIamPolicy` events granting primitive roles in last 90d.

deploy-bot: org-scan: scanned 420 projects 93 flagged 58 projects with user or SA primitive bindings. 19 service accounts have >50 permissions and likely need a permission boundary. Full CSV posted to #security-scans. :warning:

bob.dev: Quick Q: will this block existing bindings immediately on 7/1 or only prevent new ones?

alice.sec: It will block creation of new primitive bindings and upgrades to primitive roles. Existing bindings will be marked for remediation; teams have the migration window to replace them. After 2026-08-01 we will start automated removal of non-exempt primitive bindings for non-critical projects.

carol.sre: We have a handful of SRE-run sa's used by older monitoring agents that rely on editor. Can SRE request a scoped exception for those while we migrate?

alice.sec: Yes. Exceptions are temporary (max 90 days) and require a mitigation plan and owner. Use the Security Exceptions form (link on Confluence) and add `exp:iam-primitive` label. We'll prioritize infra exceptions and coordinate rollouts.

dave.eng: I can help write a small tool to convert terraform `google_project_iam_binding` entries into least-privilege custom roles and propose PRs. Would that be helpful?

alice.sec: Absolutely. Please coordinate with @infra-automation. If you submit automation, add `security-automation` tag; we will whitelist generated PRs during scans.

bob.dev: Any guidance for third-party integrations (CI providers, vendor service accounts)?

alice.sec: Vendors must use narrowly scoped roles or dedicated project-level roles. If a vendor cannot support scoped roles, file an exception and include network-level protections and TTLs. We will not accept vendor-owned SAs with owner/editor bindings.

eve.vpsec: Thanks for leading this. This policy is a big step toward reducing over-privilege across the org and is required for audit posture. We'll escalate migration blockers to team leads after 2026-06-20.

alice.sec: Runbook/status: we'll publish a migration playbook with sample TF/Cloud IAM diffs and a remediation checklist by EOD tomorrow. Ping me for repo-specific help. :lock:
